nodes.name: WhatsApp Reply Webhook
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED, fuller placeholder: this entire workflow captures RSVP/payment quick-reply button taps, but every field name below is inferred from Sendchamp's public WhatsApp docs and the underlying Meta Cloud API's typical interactive-reply shape, not confirmed against a live payload. Some WhatsApp Business Platform integrations also require a one-time GET verification handshake (hub.challenge echo) before POST events start flowing — if Sendchamp's webhook subscription needs that, add a second Webhook node (GET, same path) that returns the 'hub.challenge' query param verbatim. Register this URL as the WhatsApp inbound webhook in your Sendchamp dashboard once live, capture one real payload, and correct 'Parse Interactive Reply' before relying on this in production.

nodes.name: Find Matching Message Log Row
nodes.notes: Matches by the echoed original message id when the provider supplies one (most reliable); otherwise falls back to the most recent sent/delivered WhatsApp message to that phone number.

parameters.query:
SELECT id AS message_log_id, broadcast_id, member_id, branch_id
FROM message_log
WHERE channel = 'whatsapp'
  AND (
    ($1 IS NOT NULL AND provider_message_id = $1)
    OR ($1 IS NULL AND recipient_address = $2 AND status IN ('sent', 'delivered'))
  )
ORDER BY sent_at DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1;

nodes.name: Interpret Reply
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED: button_id conventions (e.g. 'rsvp_yes' / 'rsvp_no' / 'payment_confirm') assume the WhatsApp template was built with those ids — must match whatever ids are actually configured on the approved template once one exists.

parameters.query: UPDATE message_log SET reply_payload = $2, replied_at = now() WHERE id = $1::uuid;
